## Two more rows of the same class, and one of them says the wrong thing out loud

Same seat, same sweep, same tip (`origin/main` `7d6439c4b`, installed `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0). Adding them here rather than opening a third card, because the class is identical — the spec applies a default the form does not state. ⛔ Not graded, not routed, no labels touched.

| node type | field | kind | form states | installed spec materialises |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `loop` | `config.iteratorVariable` | `text` | `placeholder: 'currentItem'`, no `defaultValue` | `LoopConfigSchema` ⇒ `iteratorVariable: 'item'` |
| `map` | `config.iteratorVariable` | `text` | `placeholder: 'item'`, no `defaultValue` | `MapConfigSchema` ⇒ `iteratorVariable: 'item'` |

```bash
node --input-type=module -e "
import * as A from '@objectstack/spec/automation';
console.log(A.LoopConfigSchema.safeParse({ collection: '{x}' }).data);
console.log(A.MapConfigSchema.safeParse({ collection: '{x}', flowName: 'f' }).data);
"
```

⭐ **`loop` is the one that matters, and it is NOT the `maxRevisions` shape triage settled.** That settlement (objectui#9109, fence 4) rests on the two values **agreeing**: `approval.maxRevisions` prints `'3'` twice and the spec also applies `3`, so the duplication is redundant rather than wrong, and it dissolves when the number control starts reading `defaultValue`. Here the two values **disagree**: the box tells the author an unset key iterates as `currentItem`, and the runtime iterates as `item`. An author who writes `{currentItem.name}` in the loop body against that hint gets an unresolved reference — the form's own hint is the wrong one.

`map` is the `maxRevisions` shape exactly — placeholder and spec agree today, by hand, with nothing holding them together.

⚠️ **Neither is fixable by declaring `defaultValue` alone, and that is the connection to the two rows in the card body.** The `defaultValue` doc comment names three read sites — `controllerAdmits`, the `boolean` control, the `select` control. A `text` control reads `placeholder`, never `defaultValue`, so a declaration on these two fields would be inert on screen today. ⇒ the minimum honest fix for `loop` is correcting the placeholder to what the spec applies; wiring the `text` and `number` controls to read `defaultValue` (the objectui#9109 fence-4 prediction) is what would let these rows be *held* rather than re-typed.

## Coverage note — how far the sweep that found these actually reached

objectui#9109's widened ledger scopes itself to node types that have at least one declaring field, so `loop`, `map` and `end` are all outside it and none of these rows can redden there. Measured on the tip, node types with a per-type config Zod and **no** materialised default at all: `create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, `get_record`, `subflow`, `decision`, `script`, `assignment`. ⛔ **NOT MEASURED:** `notify`, `parallel`, `try_catch` — their config Zods refuse a minimal parse on required keys I did not construct, so whether they materialise defaults is unknown, ⛔ not "none". `start` has no `StartConfigSchema` export, so there is nothing to reconcile there.

## Dispatch — `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`), round R33

Claimed: objectstack-ai/objectui#9277 — dispatched to an `os-dev` seat by the `domain:ui` PM seat (`os-tesla`) at R33.
Clause-②: yes

### ⛔ This card has THREE comments — read every one (rule 38)
`5645608587` (two more rows of the same class, added by an execution seat) · `5646726264` (**the binding triage**: grading, the reversed-direction argument, the acceptance) · `5646739101` (**a cross-card conflict over a shared pin**). Where they differ from anything below, they win.

### ⭐ Premise re-verified at this seat before dispatch (rule 52)
```
flow-node-config.ts:766   cfg('lockRecord', 'Lock record', 'boolean', { help: … })        ← no defaultValue
flow-node-config.ts:927   at('boundaryConfig', 'interrupting', 'Interrupting', 'boolean', { help: … })   ← no defaultValue
FlowNodeInspector.declaredDefault.test.tsx:602   it('exactly ten fields declare a defaultValue, …
```
⇒ both absences are live and the shared pin still reads **ten**.

### ⭐ Why this is rulable while its sibling objectui#9109 is not — the two are **opposite halves**
| | objectui#9109 (`needs-user-decision`) | **this card** |
|:--|:--|:--|
| shape | the form **declares** a default the spec **does not apply** | the form **declares nothing** while the spec **applies `true`** |
| why | deleting the declaration loses `showWhen`'s reveal; backfilling needs upstream ⇒ two opposite ends | — |
| rulable? | ⛔ no | ✅ **yes** — adding a declaration equal to the value the spec **already materialises** is stating a contract the tree **already declares** ⇒ pulling back, ⛔ not widening |

⭐ And triage dismissed the card's own hesitation ("it creates an on-screen claim where none existed") with a measurement: since objectui#8451 the `boolean` control **seeds its checked state from `defaultValue`**, so "no declaration" renders **not as "no claim" but as "unchecked"**. ⇒ the screen is **already asserting something false**; declaring it turns a lie into the truth.

### The harm
An author sees `Lock record` **unchecked** and believes the record stays editable during approval — the runtime **locks it**. Sees `Interrupting` **unchecked** and believes the boundary event will **not** cancel the host activity — **it will**. ⇒ both are *the author's understanding being the opposite of the runtime's behaviour*, and `lockRecord` carries an edit-permission flavour.

### ⚠️⚠️ CROSS-CARD CONFLICT — read before you touch the pin
`FlowNodeInspector.declaredDefault.test.tsx:602` is an **exact-count** assertion, currently **ten**. Two cards move it, and **objectui#9278 is IN FLIGHT RIGHT NOW**:

| card | declarations added | number that card wrote for itself |
|:--|--:|--:|
| **this card** (`lockRecord` + `interrupting`) | **2** | 10 → **12** |
| objectui#9278 (`end.outcome`), **live this round** | 1 | 10 → **11** |

Both are right in isolation. Both landing ⇒ the truth is **13**, and whichever lands second meets a red pin it did not expect.

⇒ ⛔ **Do NOT write "12" into the implementation.** Compute **the pin's value at the moment you land, plus your own 2**, and **say in the PR body where you read the base from**. ⚠️ The "12" this card wrote was computed assuming objectui#9278 does not exist. ⭐ The pin's own comment says *"a PR that … adds an eleventh declaration, moves this line"* ⇒ reddening it is **expected**; ⛔ do not route around it, and **update the comment along with the count**.

### The acceptance
- Both fields get `defaultValue: 'true'` — the **string spelling this table uses** (the one `controllerAdmits` compares against), ⭐ **derived from the installed spec**, per the `defaultValue` doc comment's *"derive it from the spec, never from taste"*.
- Pin count per the conflict rule above; comment updated with it.
- ⭐ **Ablation leg**: drop either `defaultValue` — that checkbox's seeding assertion must redden.
- ⚠️ **If objectui#9109's `UNDECLARED_REGISTER` has landed by then**, delete those two register rows in the same PR or the ledger goes red. ⭐ **Measured just now: 0 hits — it has NOT landed.** ⇒ if it still has not, ⛔ **do not invent one**.
- ⚠️ Per objectui#9273, a package-scoped run is not the blast radius — something rendered moves ⇒ `examples/schema-catalog/` and count-shaped prose figures.

### ⚠️ One thing triage did NOT measure — verify it yourself
The spec side (`ApprovalNodeConfigSchema` materialising `lockRecord: true`; the `FlowNodeSchema` block materialising `interrupting: true`) is **NOT MEASURED** by triage — `@objectstack/spec` was not installed there. The card supplies a probe **with a positive control in the same output** (`behavior` / `onEmptyApprovers` / `maxRevisions` do have matching form declarations). ⭐ Run it and report which way it read — your two option values come from that answer.

### ⛔ Out of scope this round, and why
Comment `5645608587` names two more rows of the same class — `loop.config.iteratorVariable` and `map.config.iteratorVariable`. ⛔ **Do not fold them in.** They are `text` controls, and the `defaultValue` doc comment names only three read sites (`controllerAdmits`, the `boolean` control, the `select` control) — **a `text` control reads `placeholder`, never `defaultValue`**, so a declaration there would be **inert on screen today**.
⭐ But `loop` is worth a measurement while you are in the file: its placeholder says `currentItem` while the spec applies **`item`** — the two **disagree**, so the form's own hint is the wrong one and an author writing `{currentItem.name}` gets an unresolved reference. ⚠️ **Measure and report it; ⛔ do not repair it here.** I will file it.

### Standing constraints for this round
- Read `AGENTS.md` in full before your first edit. ⛔ `packages/components/src/ui/**/*.tsx` is a **No-Touch zone** (Commandment #7).
- ⛔ Never skip, disable or quarantine a test. ⛔ Never force-push or rewrite pushed history.
- **Changeset required.** 41 packages in ONE `fixed` group ⇒ `major` unavailable; breaking ships as `minor` with a `**BREAKING**` carrier. Justify by **measurement** — two checkboxes change their rendered state.
- ⚠️ There is **no npm script matching `no-major`**; the file runs inside **`changeset:check`**.
- objectui has **no** `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`; derive the gate family by hand from `package.json` + `.github/workflows/`.
- ⚠️⚠️ **A declared narrowing of your verification union can still be the load-bearing one.** This lane paid for it: a seat excluded `@object-ui/site` as "a docs app", but `apps/site` declares `type-check` **and** depends on the package under change — CI went red exactly there. ⭐ Do a **membership read** of the dependent set before trusting any exclusion. (Two seats did this correctly this round.)
- ⚠️ **Install/build first.** A missing `node_modules` makes every `require.resolve` fail identically — **instrument failure, not a negative answer**. Read verdicts from the verify-lock wrapper's VERDICT line, never a bare `$?`.
- ⭐ **⛔ A grep truncated by `head` is not a zero reading.** Triage logged that exact slip on this very pin: `grep … | head -12` cut off the line it was looking for and it briefly read the two cards as citing a comment that does not exist.
- ⚠️ **Carrier rule (directional):** hang `needs:contract-review` on **both** limbs in one stroke. ⛔ **Never clear either limb**; clearing is the PM's. (REST label POST needs `Content-Type: application/json`, else **415**.)
- ⚠️ **In flight:** **objectui#9278 is editing the same file and the same pin** — coordinate by computing from the live value, ⛔ not by assuming you are first. Also objectui#9304 (`plugin-detail`, `plugin-form`), PRs objectui#9325 / #9326 (queued), PR objectui#9310 (held).
- ⛔ No model identifier in any pushed artifact; ⛔ don't copy a neighbouring commit's trailer — use the model-free form. ⛔ Card relations belong in the **PR body**, not the commit message.

### ⭐ The two instrument standards this seat holds
1. **Write the pin BEFORE the code** — the "unmodified" arm is then the real base tree.
2. **Every control must be able to fire.** ⭐ The card's probe is the model: the three rows that **do** have matching declarations appear in the **same output** as the two that do not, which is what makes the absences a reading rather than a dead probe.
